item.title: Apple TV is adapting Brandon Sanderson’s The Cosmere universe
item.description: The success of sci-fi series such as For All Mankind, Severance, Foundation, Silo and Pluribus has clearly encouraged Apple TV to go big. The service has acquired the rights to the Cosmere universe, created by the acclaimed fantasy writer Brandon Sanderson. The platform intends to adapt the Mistborn novels into features and to create a TV show based on The Stormlight Archive series. item.title: The truth is, Android 17 won’t matter to most people
item.description: Android is almost two decades old, but it still suffers from the same big problem. While the latest version, Android 16, is available on all supported Google Pixel phones and many of the other best phones around, its rollout to older handsets continues at a glacial pace. item.title: 9 million Android devices hijacked in secret proxy network
item.description: Google announced that it has shut down what the company describes as the world’s largest residential proxy network. Chinese company IPIDEA is believed to be behind the network and, according to Google, around nine million Android devices were hijacked, along with computers and smart home products. The revelation was first reported by our sister publication PC-Welt. The hijacking took place via hidden code libraries, known as SDKs, which were built into over 600 free apps and programs. item.title: Sky is bringing back this iconic British channel
item.description: Remember Sky One – the British channel that launched in the 1980s, and was home to many original programmes and American series? Well, it’s coming back, bringing together well-known and completely new shows. During its 39 years, the channel broadcast British hits such as The Russell Howard Hour and An Idiot Abroad, and allowed viewers to catch up on the likes of The X-Files, The Simpsons, The Middle and Star Trek.
